name: CR2032

codes.note: Rechargeable lithium-ion battery in the same case; 3.6 V, and does not work in place of a CR2032 in devices built for 3 V

dimensions.note: Minimum and maximum limits from the Energizer engineering datasheet; Panasonic publishes the same maximums. Negative contact is at least 8.0 mm in diameter.

negative.note: Minimum diameter of the flat negative contact area per Energizer.

capacity_mah.conditions: Panasonic nominal capacity at 0.2 mA continuous standard drain; cutoff voltage not stated

variants.notes: Energizer lists 225 mAh at 10 kΩ to 2.0 V, Varta 230 mAh, GP 220 mAh. Lithium content per Energizer. Weights run 2.8 g (Panasonic) to 3.3 g (Energizer).

variants.label: BR2032

capacity_mah.conditions: Panasonic nominal capacity at 0.03 mA continuous standard drain; cutoff not stated

variants.notes: BR2032 is a lithium-carbon-monofluoride cell in the same case. It has a flatter discharge curve and lower pulse capability than the CR type, and lower rated drain.

variants.label: LIR2032

capacity_mah.conditions: PowerStream catalog nominal capacity; load and cutoff not stated on the page

variants.notes: The LIR2032 is a lithium-ion cell at 3.6 V nominal that charges to a higher voltage than a CR2032 supplies. It is not a drop-in replacement for a CR2032 in a device built for 3 V, and a CR2032 must not be placed in a holder designed to charge a LIR2032.

interchange.note: Same 20 mm width and 0.7 mm thinner; lower capacity, and thinner batteries can make poor contact in a CR2032 holder.
Same 20 mm width and 1.6 mm thinner; much lower capacity, and thinner batteries can make poor contact in a CR2032 holder.
Same 3.2 mm thickness, but 30 mm across instead of 20 mm; does not fit a CR2032 holder.

notes: The most widely used lithium coin cell. BR2032 has the same dimensions and a nominal 3 V but lower rated drain and a wider temperature range; ML2032 and VL2032 are rechargeable cells in the same case per Wikipedia, and fit the same holder only where the device is designed to charge them.

safety: Swallowed coin batteries can cause severe internal burns within two hours. Keep batteries away from children, and seek emergency medical care immediately if one is swallowed or placed in the nose or ears.
In the United States, the National Battery Ingestion Hotline is 1-800-498-8666 and Poison Help is 1-800-222-1222.
Do not recharge, crush, puncture, heat or short-circuit a single-use lithium coin battery.
